title: Management and Leadership for Compliance and Risk Teams
summary: A ten-module programme giving managers of compliance, risk and financial crime teams the skills to lead the second line, influence the business and earn the board's confidence.
intro: This training programme equips managers and heads of compliance, risk and financial crime teams with the leadership skills to run an effective second line: influencing without authority, challenging the business, managing performance and building credibility with the board.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give managers in compliance, risk and financial crime functions the people and leadership skills that technical expertise alone does not provide, in a role where they must challenge colleagues who outrank them and out-earn them. Participants leave able to lead and develop a second-line team, prioritise a demanding risk-based workload, influence and challenge the business, and earn the confidence of senior management, the board and the supervisor.
sections.What It Covers: The move from specialist to second-line manager, influence without authority, challenging the business, prioritisation and resourcing, delegation and performance management, coaching and developing control function staff, reporting upward to executives and the board, credibility with the board and the supervisor, wellbeing and resilience under pressure, and leading through change and incidents.
Intended Audience: Compliance, risk and financial crime specialists newly promoted, or preparing for promotion, into team leader and manager roles
Heads of compliance, chief risk officers, MLROs and their deputies seeking to strengthen how they lead and position the function
Senior managers who lead other control or assurance teams, or who sponsor the second line within the business
Learning Objectives: Explain how the role changes from control function specialist to second-line manager and leader
Apply influencing and challenge techniques to change business decisions without line authority
Prioritise and resource the team's workload by risk, and manage performance fairly and early
Develop team members' judgement and confidence through coaching, feedback and delegation
Report upward to executives and the board in a way that drives decisions and builds credibility
Lead the team through pressure, incidents and change while protecting wellbeing, and agree a personal leadership plan
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions spread over several months. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, self-assessment, role-play and skills practice, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's control function structure and leadership framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience in a compliance, risk or financial crime role is helpful. No prior management training is required.
Core Reading: Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Patrick Lencioni, The Five Dysfunctions of a Team (2002)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)

modules.title: From Specialist to Second-Line Manager
modules.summary: The shift from being the technical expert who gives the answer to leading a team that the business must respect, and what changes in accountability, visibility and relationships on promotion.
objectives: Explain how the second-line manager role differs from the specialist role
Assess personal strengths and development needs as a control function manager
Establish credibility and clear expectations with a new team and with business peers
syllabus: From doing to enabling: what changes on promotion
The particular position of the second line: independent, but part of the firm
Managing former peers and setting team expectations
Self-assessment: management style and development priorities

modules.title: Influence Without Authority
modules.summary: How control function managers persuade business heads and executives who do not report to them, by mapping stakeholders, understanding commercial pressures and framing advice so it is acted upon.
objectives: Map and prioritise stakeholders across the business, executives and the board
Frame regulatory and risk advice in terms the business values
Build relationships that preserve influence without compromising independence
syllabus: Sources of influence for the second line: expertise, trust and the board's mandate
Understanding commercial drivers, targets and incentives in the business
Framing advice: risk, outcome and options rather than prohibition
Avoiding capture: when closeness to the business becomes a risk

modules.title: Challenging the Business
modules.summary: How to deliver effective challenge to senior colleagues on products, deals, controls and incidents, handle pushback and seniority, and know when to hold a line and when to escalate.
objectives: Distinguish effective challenge from objection, obstruction and box-ticking
Apply evidence-based techniques to challenge senior colleagues with confidence
Decide when to escalate and record challenge so that it can be evidenced
syllabus: What effective challenge looks like to the board and the supervisor
Preparing a challenge: evidence, risk, options and the ask
Handling pushback, commercial pressure and appeals to seniority
Role-play: challenging a business head on a new product launch

modules.title: Prioritisation, Resourcing and the Risk-Based Workload
modules.summary: How to set the team's priorities when demand always exceeds capacity, make the case for resources, and say no to low-value work without leaving the firm exposed.
objectives: Apply risk-based prioritisation to competing advisory, monitoring and regulatory demands
Build a credible case for headcount, skills and tools
Agree with senior management what the function will not do and record the risk
syllabus: Prioritisation tools linked to the compliance and risk assessment
Regulatory change, incidents and business requests: managing the peaks
Making the resourcing case: workload data, risk and supervisory expectations
Saying no and accepting residual risk transparently

modules.title: Delegation and Managing Performance
modules.summary: How to delegate control work with clear outcomes and quality standards, set meaningful objectives for second-line staff, and address underperformance fairly and early.
objectives: Delegate work with clear outcomes, authority, checkpoints and sign-off standards
Set objectives that reward quality of judgement rather than volume of activity
Manage underperformance and difficult people issues fairly and early
syllabus: Effective delegation: what, to whom and how much review
Objectives and measures for control function staff
Performance conversations, including underperformance
Quality assurance of the team's work without rewriting it

modules.title: Coaching and Developing Control Function Staff
modules.summary: How to build judgement, confidence and resilience in compliance, risk and financial crime staff through coaching conversations, feedback and planned development.
objectives: Apply a structured coaching model in everyday management
Give feedback that is specific, balanced and actionable
Plan development and succession for key roles in the function
syllabus: Coaching models and powerful questions
Building judgement: talking through the reasoning, not just the answer
Development paths, qualifications and rotation into the business
Skills practice: a coaching conversation

modules.title: Reporting Upward to Executives and the Board
modules.summary: How to write papers and reports for executive committees, risk and audit committees and the board that lead with the message, frame the decision and give an honest view of risk.
objectives: Structure a paper or report around the decision or assurance required
Present an honest view of risk and control weaknesses without alarm or comfort
Handle challenging questions from executives and directors
syllabus: Writing for decision: the one-page summary and recommendation
Function reports that inform: themes, trends and risk appetite rather than activity
Presenting to committees: message first, evidence second
Skills practice: a short briefing to a mock risk committee

modules.title: Building Credibility with the Board and the Supervisor
modules.summary: How control function leaders build standing with the chair, committee chairs and non-executive directors, use their independent access well, and represent the function in supervisory engagement.
objectives: Use independent access to the board and committee chairs effectively
Position the function as a trusted source of judgement for the board
Lead the team's engagement with supervisors with candour and consistency
syllabus: The relationship with the chair, committee chairs and non-executive directors
Private sessions and raising concerns the executive would prefer not heard
How supervisors judge the standing and independence of control functions
Leading the team through a supervisory visit or thematic review

modules.title: Wellbeing, Resilience and Sustainable Performance
modules.summary: The particular pressures of second-line work, including isolation, conflict with the business, personal accountability and incident peaks, and how managers protect their own and the team's resilience.
objectives: Explain the specific pressures of control function roles
Recognise early warning signs of stress and burnout in self and others
Apply practical techniques to build personal and team resilience
syllabus: Sources of pressure: conflict, accountability, workload and incidents
Psychological safety and speaking up within the function
Workload design and the manager's role in wellbeing
A personal and team resilience plan

modules.title: Leading Through Incidents and Change: Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a simulated incident and change scenario, followed by a personal leadership plan covering direction for the team, accountability and continuing development.
objectives: Lead a team through a time-pressured incident and communicate decisions clearly
Plan and sustain change in the function's structure, tools or approach
Produce a personal leadership development plan
syllabus: Decision-making under pressure: bias, incomplete information and ownership
Leading change: new regulation, restructuring and technology in the second line
Simulation: a breach escalating to the board and the supervisor
Workshop: the twelve-month personal leadership plan
